title: The New York Times warns photographers not to update Photoshop over AI features
lede: The New York Times told freelance photographers to avoid Photoshop 2027 because its AI features can attach C2PA metadata marking photos as AI-edited, even after minimal edits.

points: The email from photo leads Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner covers release 28.0.0 and all later updates for Times assignments.
Adobe's November update adds an AI Assisted Editor toolbar, prompt-based edits, AI upscaling and AI recomposition for new canvas sizes.
It is unclear which tools count as AI; even older automated selection may now be labelled that way.
Adobe started adding C2PA metadata across its apps in August, and the Times wants those labels kept off its photos.

points.text: A creative-tools worker says metadata cannot tell a small AI touch-up from a fully generated image, and an AI label can sink an authoritative brand's credibility.
Several describe a wider stigma: many people actively dislike AI imagery, so any link to it is a liability.
One commenter asks how healing brush or content-aware fill differ from generative models, since all of them invent pixels.
Some say the Times could screen metadata in its own CMS instead of banning a tool; a reply says it wants to avoid rejecting whole photo sets.
